title: TDL-2 — Tag Primary Document And Semantic Token Delivery
summary: replace Tag Registry membership editing with ordered document pills, an optional primary override, and deterministic Tag Semantic Tokens
content_html:
TDL-2 — Tag Primary Document And Semantic Token Delivery

Status And Purpose

TDL-2.0 scope review is complete in the Tag Document Linking sequence and is associated with Semantic Tokens. The delivery is parked before TDL-2.1 implementation approval. TDL-1 is complete; TDL-2 replaces tag_registry_v5.doc_url[] membership editing with its shipped complete ordered read-only reverse lookup and one optional Registry-owned primary_document override.

The delivery also adds Tag as a second Semantic Tokens family. It keeps Tag separate from Catalogue: a Work or Series resolves to one concrete catalogue destination, while a Tag resolves to its exact current primary override or otherwise the first current document in TDL-1's deterministic association order.

Current Implementation Fit — 11 August 2026

TDL-1 now supplies optional document-owned tag_id, normalized missing/valid/malformed evidence, the private deterministic docs_tag_associations_v1 product with exact ordered targets and optional locations, and the current-source ordinary Delete Tag guard. The product is stable and private but currently empty: 249 managed Tag documents have no declarations, while tag_registry_v5 retains 247 canonical Tags and 246 legacy document URLs. TDL-2 must migrate those links into declarations, validate the resulting association product, and remove Registry membership ownership before primary selection or Tag token work begins.

The live migration reconciliation resolves 245 legacy URLs to 245 distinct current public Tag documents with no duplicate target and no current multi-document Registry row. bird-nerve has the sole unresolved legacy URL, while aaa has no legacy URL. Three other public Tag documents and one unpublished Tag document have no exact legacy Registry association and must not be inferred into the migration. The resulting current migration therefore proposes 245 exact tag_id declarations and no primary_document values; unresolved and unassociated evidence remains explicit for review.

The current semantic registry exposes Catalogue Work and Series targets only; Moment has retired. Catalogue target records have since gained image context and Work detail availability, but each target still resolves through the same single safe href, so Tag needs neither a shared target schema expansion nor Catalogue coupling. The family registry, normalized target lookup, guarded Source range mutation, usage index, and report already carry family identity; the target builder, Markdown parser/renderer, browser Info contribution, and Broken Links semantic scan remain Catalogue-specific and need bounded Tag contributions rather than a new schema or generic plugin framework. The migration and primary-selection cutover must complete and be verified before the Tag family is registered or parsed, keeping canonical data migration separate from semantic implementation.

The ordinary Delete Tag path revalidates current document source rather than the generated association or Registry link fields, so neither migrated nor stale primary_document state participates in deletion eligibility. The live Demote Tag path also removes the canonical Tag but does not yet use that guard; TDL-2.1 must apply the same source-owned block to both canonical-removal actions before migration, without rewriting or deleting documents.

Complete Outcome

In Manage Source, an author selects meaningful text, chooses Add tag token, searches canonical Tags and aliases, and selects one exact canonical tag_id. The built document converts the authored text to the Tag's current resolved document link:

[Nerve]

The source records stable Tag identity rather than copying document URLs. A normal rebuild reads the ordered derived Tag associations: a current associated primary overrides the list, otherwise the first current association is selected automatically. The rebuild records one Tag-token occurrence in the scope usage index. The public document contains ordinary resolved links and no Tag Registry, target lookup, or client-side semantic resolver.

Fixed Product Direction

Separate Family And Action

  • Tag is a separate Semantic Tokens family with its own Add tag token action, discovery modal, parser contribution, and Info view.
  • Tag is not added to Add catalogue token search. Catalogue continues to combine only Work and Series.
  • The Tag family reuses the generic source selection, guarded range mutation, modal lifecycle, token registry, target lookup, build projection, usage index, report, and Broken Links seams.
  • The canonical identity is tag_id. Aliases are discovery inputs only and always resolve to a selected canonical Tag.
  • Group and the current resolved-document title are distinguishing lookup context; they are not copied into source identity.

Resolved Association Is The Target

  • A Tag target is a current associated Registry primary when one is selected, or otherwise the first current association in TDL-1's stable ascending {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} order. There is no separate Tag landing page.
  • TDL-1 document declarations own association membership and canonical order. The Tag Registry editor displays the complete ordered list read-only and remains authoritative for canonical Tag identity, group, aliases, and the optional primary override. Semantic Tokens consume a focused generated target projection and do not inspect or mutate canonical Tag JSON directly.
  • Document-location projection supplies current public-safe titles and URLs. A token never infers an association from document title, content, current route, report host, or neighbouring source.

Wrapped Selection

The action replaces the captured selection with a token containing the occurrence text:

[[tag:tag:nerve|nerve]]

The builder renders:

[Nerve]

The token owns both the visible occurrence text and Tag identity; its Info view can edit the occurrence text while keeping identity readonly.

Link Resolution

  • A recognized Tag token resolves from the canonical Tag row and its exact current TDL-1 association set according to this fixed matrix:
Current associated documents Resolution
None Unresolved.
One Use that first and sole document; no primary override is required.
Several, with a current associated primary_document Use that exact selected document.
Several, without a current associated primary_document Use the first document in TDL-1's deterministic association order.
  • The occurrence Title stored in the token is the rendered anchor label. The associated document title may appear as discovery or Info context but does not replace the authored Title.
  • Retained doc_url[] data is a migration input only. TDL-2 replaces canonical association membership with TDL-1's derived document declarations; focused consumers may use the complete derived association set.
  • Candidate selection happens before location resolution. A stored primary absent from the current association set is not a current override, so selection returns to the canonical first document. Once the exact candidate is selected, a missing, unpublished, or otherwise unusable public-safe location leaves the token unresolved rather than scanning later associations.
  • The default-first rule is deliberate product behavior, not inferred relevance: titles, availability, recent use, semantic-token usage, Registry ordering, and current UI state never choose the document. Unresolved source remains ordinary text, creates no resolved usage row, and can be diagnosed by Docs Broken Links.
  • Public output is resolved at build time into one ordinary anchor. Public readers receive no Tag Registry, target lookup, usage index, or resolution runtime.

Tag Registry Document Pills And Primary Override

The Tag Registry editor displays all current TDL-1 associations as document pills in canonical association order and treats membership and ordering as read-only. It cannot search for, add, remove, or reorder documents; only editing or deleting document source changes the list. The document label opens that exact Docs Viewer target. The pill has no × or other association-removal control.

Each current document pill has a trailing accessible radio-style circle. A hollow circle means the document is not the stored primary override; the one selected primary has a filled circle. Activating a hollow circle drafts that exact document as primary_document. If every circle is hollow, Semantic Tokens use the first displayed document automatically. Once a primary has been stored, the editor offers no clear action: selecting another pill replaces it, while activating the already-filled circle leaves it selected. The next Registry schema stores:

{
  "primary_document": {
    "scope": "analysis",
    "sub_scope": "tags",
    "doc_id": "d-..."
  }
}

primary_document is optional and scalar. It is not a URL or association list and is never required for Semantic Token resolution when current associations exist.

  • The association list is a read-only TDL-1 projection. The editor never writes membership back to documents or Registry association fields.
  • With no associated document, the editor shows the empty state. With one, it shows the sole pill and its circle; leaving the circle hollow uses that first and sole document automatically, so no Studio selection is required.
  • With one or several documents, the current pill circles form one accessible single-selection group. The initially empty automatic state or a selected identity is committed by the existing atomic Tag mutation boundary. Once selected, a primary can only be replaced by another current pill or removed with the complete Tag row. These are only the already-associated records supplied by TDL-1; this is not general document search.
  • If a stored primary is absent from the reverse lookup because its document was deleted or reassigned, migration input is stale, or an out-of-band source change occurred, its exact identity remains visible separately as Unavailable document and every current pill circle remains hollow. Semantic resolution treats the absent primary as no current override and uses the first current pill. Selecting a current circle replaces the stale value; if no association exists, the stale identity remains until the Tag itself is deleted.
  • Selection changes remain draft operations until Save. Close discards them.
  • The pills preserve TDL-1 order so the first visible document is the automatic semantic destination. Title sorting, availability sorting, recently-used ranking, semantic-token usage, and Registry draft order cannot change that sequence.
  • Selecting or replacing the primary changes whether the Tag Semantic Token destination is overridden or automatic. It does not transfer document lifecycle ownership to Tag Registry, synchronize a document with Tag identity, or participate in document or Tag deletion eligibility.
  • Tag Registry remains the canonical Tag definition for Work tagging: canonical identity, group, aliases, and primary document stay Registry-owned. Documents own their declarations and may cross-reference one another in their content.

Registry Migration

TDL-2 performs one bounded migration from tag_registry_v5.doc_url[] after TDL-1's Tag declaration and reverse-lookup contracts are available:

  • every exact legacy association is converted into the corresponding document's tag_id declaration where the target can be resolved and safely updated;
  • when the resulting reverse lookup contains several current associations, the exact identity represented by doc_url[0] becomes primary_document only if it is one of them; otherwise it is reported for review, and zero or one current association requires no migrated primary;
  • later doc_url[] entries contribute only to document declarations and do not remain in the Registry row;
  • unresolvable or conflicting legacy entries are reported for review rather than inferred, dropped silently, or turned into free-form URLs;
  • the generated reverse lookup is compared with the migration plan before commit; and
  • doc_url[] is removed after the scalar primary and reverse lookup are validated, with no continuing dual-write or dual-read compatibility layer.

Target And Usage Projection

The current Semantic Tokens target row already assumes one workable href. Tag can reuse that shape without a multi-target schema: the focused Tag projection derives one candidate from the exact current primary override or canonical first association, then emits one workable href or no resolved row.

A proposed Tag target row contains:

{
  "family": "tag",
  "target_type": "tag",
  "target_id": "nerve",
  "title": "nerve",
  "href": "/analysis/?doc=...&subdoc=...",
  "meta": ["subject", "Nerve"]
}

The exact field names and unavailable-record representation remain bounded implementation decisions within the existing Semantic Tokens target owner. Required semantics are:

  • one lookup row per canonical Tag whose exact selected-primary-or-first candidate has a workable public-safe location under the zero/one/several matrix;
  • one safe href resolved from that exact stored document identity;
  • canonical aliases available to discovery without becoming target identity;
  • the canonical group and associated document title available only as compact lookup context where useful;
  • one ordinary resolved usage occurrence per authored Tag token; and
  • exact source document and source range for report navigation and targeted build preservation.

The Semantic Tokens report treats Tag like another resolved family occurrence and links back to its source document. Docs Broken Links remains the read-only diagnosis owner for unknown Tags, zero associations, and unusable selected-primary-or-first destinations.

Delivery Discipline

TDL-2 is one complete second-family vertical slice over the existing single-target Semantic Tokens contract. It should add a focused Tag lookup adapter and family-owned UI without introducing multi-target schema, rendering, or report behavior. It must not turn the registry into executable plugins, combine Tag and Catalogue search, add a generic graph, create a public Tag application, give the Tag Editor association-mutation authority, or move primary-override selection into Docs Viewer.

TDL-2.0 is a short scope-and-spec sanity gate over Tag migration, primary selection, target projection, Source authoring, build/usage, reports, and public isolation. It confirms broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, and stop conditions without freezing exact files, fixtures, estimates, or implementation. Each implementation stage ends with focused evidence and an independent code/diff review. Any proposed expansion of the existing single-href contract is a pause-and-review signal because this delivery does not require it.

Likely Authority To Inspect

This is a routing map for delivery work, not a required entry audit or frozen file-change list.

boundary likely current owners delivery pressure
family definition and browser registry docs-viewer/config/semantic-tokens/registry.json and source-editor/semantic-token-registry.js register Tag without adding it to Catalogue discovery
canonical Tag identity and primary selection studio/data/canonical/tags/ and studio/services/tags/ replace doc_url[] membership with optional primary override while retaining canonical Work-tagging authority
primary editing and association validation TDL-1 reverse lookup plus studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-* display ordered read-only document pills, preserve exact navigation, and replace each removal × with an accessible primary circle
document lifecycle independence Docs Viewer exact document Delete and Analysis Tags field assignment plus the TDL-1 association rebuild never read or mutate primary_document; retain any removed selected identity as stale Registry evidence
target lookup docs_builder/semantic_target_lookup.py and Semantic Token target adapters derive the existing single safe href from the exact current primary or deterministic first association, without scanning for a more attractive member
source authoring and Info generic Source contribution/range seams plus new Tag-owned modules beside catalogue-token-* wrap the captured selection and keep Tag identity readonly
build and usage docs_builder/semantic_tokens.py and semantic_token_artifacts.py reuse ordinary single-link rendering and one resolved occurrence
reports and diagnosis Semantic Tokens report and Docs Broken Links semantic checks show the Tag occurrence and diagnose zero, stale-primary evidence, or unavailable chosen targets
assurance shared grammar fixtures, focused Python contracts, and browser module smoke prove the Tag family while protecting Catalogue behavior and rejecting multi-association projection

Delivery Steps

TDL-2.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [x] Sanity-check the ordered read-only document pills, optional scalar-primary migration, deterministic first-document default, and single-link Semantic Token outcome against the accepted TDL-1 association contract and current Tag Registry, document-location, Semantic Tokens, Source editing, usage/reporting, and Broken Links models; resolve only contradictions that would change the result.
  • [x] Confirm the broad blast radius across canonical Tag migration/read/write/import, document tag_id declarations, replace-only primary editing, primary-independent document lifecycle mutations, focused target projection, Source authoring/Info, build rendering, usage preservation, reports, and public isolation.
  • [x] Confirm the deliverables: complete ordered read-only document pills with no removal control, exact navigation labels, accessible primary circles, one optional replace-only override, automatic first-document resolution for empty or stale primary state, the zero/one/several target projection, wrapped Tag token authoring, single-anchor build/usage, bounded migration evidence, focused verification, and concise durable owner updates.
  • [x] Stop for review if the result requires multi-target Semantic Tokens, Tag Editor membership mutation or reordering, dual-read/write compatibility, inferred membership, title- or availability-derived ordering, scanning for a preferred later association, combined Tag/Catalogue discovery, a public Tag application, or another boundary excluded above. Do not produce an exact file inventory, line estimate, frozen implementation, fixture implementation, or complete test architecture at this gate.

Checkpoint: a concise sanity note confirms the spec, TDL-1 dependency, broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, migration/public boundary, and stop condition. Stop before TDL-2.1 implementation approval.

TDL-2.0 Sanity Note — 11 August 2026

The accepted product direction fits the live TDL-1 contracts without changing its ownership model. Document source remains the sole association-membership owner; the private association product remains the sole canonical-order owner; Registry owns only canonical Tag data and an optional exact scalar primary override; and Semantic Tokens resolve one candidate to one ordinary link. Empty or stale primary state uses the first current association, while an unusable chosen candidate remains unresolved rather than causing a later-association scan.

The Registry cutover is a reviewed data migration rather than an editor-driven repair. A fingerprinted preview must show the 245 exact source edits, the sole unresolved bird-nerve URL, the deliberately unlinked aaa row, every unrelated unassociated document, the projected primary result, and the complete derived association comparison before apply. Apply removes doc_url[] without a dual reader or writer, preserves unresolved evidence in the reviewed migration record rather than canonical Registry membership, and completes the Registry schema cutover before primary UI becomes available.

TDL-2.1 reuses the canonical Registry validator/mutation transaction, TDL-1 declaration projector and private association, a bounded private Studio read seam, and the existing Tag Editor modal/draft/save boundary. It retires public document search and add/remove controls, validates only a newly selected exact current primary, preserves an omitted or stale stored primary during unrelated edits, and applies the declaration guard to both Delete Tag and Demote Tag. Docs Viewer document mutations remain entirely primary-blind.

TDL-2.2 and TDL-2.3 reuse the family-aware registry, single-href lookup row, guarded Source range mutation, usage receipt, report, and Broken Links owners while adding focused Tag target, text-token, discovery, and Info contributions. The full delivery is expected to be a data-heavy migration plus several hundred bounded production and focused-test lines; that shape is acceptable only while it remains within these existing owners. A compatibility layer, generalized plugin engine, multi-target contract, inferred migration, public canonical data, or broader Catalogue refactor is a stop-and-review condition.

TDL-2.1 — Registry Migration And Primary Selection

  • [ ] Apply the reviewed migration plan to exact Tag documents and replace Registry doc_url[] with optional scalar primary_document without a dual-write compatibility period.
  • [ ] Generate and validate the complete TDL-1 reverse lookup before accepting migrated Registry rows; report unresolved legacy associations without inventing membership.
  • [ ] Update canonical Tag read/write/import contracts to retain identity, group, aliases, and optional primary-override authority for Work tagging while removing Registry-owned association membership.
  • [ ] Apply the same current-source association block to Delete Tag and Demote Tag before either action removes a canonical Tag; neither action may rewrite or delete document source.
  • [ ] Replace Tag Editor association mutation controls with complete ordered read-only TDL-1 document pills: the label opens the exact document, the removal × is absent, and each current pill has a hollow or filled accessible primary circle.
  • [ ] Preserve the first displayed document as the automatic destination when no current circle is selected, allow a stored primary to be replaced only by selecting another current pill, and keep all selector changes within the existing atomic Registry mutation boundary without document search, a clear action, or a multi-document draft.
  • [ ] Preserve a deleted or otherwise unknown stored primary visibly until the user selects a current replacement or deletes the complete Tag row.
  • [ ] Keep document Delete and tag_id assignment, reassignment, or clear independent of primary state: rebuild exact associations, retain a removed selected identity as Unavailable document, and never block, clear, replace, or otherwise mutate Registry primary state from Docs Viewer.
  • [ ] Verify the migrated declarations, complete ordered private associations, zero/one/several pill states, hollow automatic state, filled selected and replacement states, keyboard and screen-reader selection semantics, unavailable stored primary, primary-independent document mutation, unresolved-entry report, and removal of the old Registry field before any Tag semantic implementation starts.

Checkpoint: focused migration, canonical Tag, ordered read-only pill list, exact navigation, zero/one/several automatic/selected/replaced primary-editor states, unavailable-primary fallback, primary-independent document mutation, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms document-owned membership and lifecycle, optional replace-only scalar primary ownership, and complete retirement of the old Registry association field without a compatibility layer. Stop before TDL-2.2.

TDL-2.2 — Single-Link Semantic Target And Build

  • [ ] Add the focused Tag target generator over canonical Registry, TDL-1 ordered associations, aliases, and the public-safe document-location projection for the exact current primary override or canonical first document.
  • [ ] Register the Tag family in the existing single-href target schema and shared consumers without adding it to Catalogue discovery.
  • [ ] Implement tolerant parsing and single-anchor build rendering for wrapped Tag tokens and the specified zero, sole-default, several-default, selected-primary, stale-primary, and unavailable-chosen-destination states.
  • [ ] Generate one ordinary resolved usage occurrence while preserving untouched documents during targeted builds.
  • [ ] Keep Tag canonical data, aliases, target lookup, and usage data out of public output.

Checkpoint: focused target lookup, parser, builder, usage, targeted-build, zero/one/several resolution, stable selected-primary-or-first choice, stale-primary fallback, no later-association scan, Catalogue-regression, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms the existing single-link contract is unchanged. Stop before TDL-2.3.

TDL-2.3 — Authoring, Info, Reports, Regression, And Transfer

  • [ ] Add the separate Add tag token Source action and Tag discovery modal with canonical ID, alias, group, and resolved-document context.
  • [ ] Insert the wrapped token through captured, revision-guarded Source mutation only.
  • [ ] Add the family-specific Info view with immutable identity, current target context, permitted occurrence editing, and exact-range removal.
  • [ ] Preserve validation, unavailable-target, and stale-range errors without adding redundant successful-mutation status messages.
  • [ ] Extend the Semantic Tokens report and Docs Broken Links diagnosis for the specified Tag occurrence and association states.
  • [ ] Prove Catalogue Work and Series insertion, Info, rendering, usage, and unresolved behaviour are unchanged.
  • [ ] Verify migration, canonical and alias discovery, zero/one/many ordered derived associations, automatic first-document resolution, selected/replaced/stale/deleted/unavailable primary overrides, primary-independent document Delete and Tag reassignment/clear, unknown-target preservation, no later-association scan after an unusable chosen destination, source edits, targeted rebuild preservation, public links, and public isolation.
  • [ ] Run focused Python, browser-module, lint, whitespace, generated docs, and search checks, then perform the independent final code/delivery and omission review.
  • [ ] Transfer shipped behaviour to the concise Semantic Tokens, Tag Registry, Source Editor UI, Architecture, Target Lookup, and Usage Index owners.

Checkpoint: focused module, route, report, regression, and public-boundary evidence passes. Manual acceptance adds a Tag token from selected prose, verifies that no filled circle resolves to the first displayed associated document, selects another pill's circle and observes that override after Save, selects a different pill to replace it, and verifies that deleting the selected document leaves Unavailable document while resolution returns to the first current association. An independent final review confirms exact identity, guarded source mutation, document-owned membership and lifecycle, replace-only primary override, and separation from Catalogue discovery.

Not In Scope

  • combining Tag targets with Catalogue discovery or the Catalogue toolbar action;
  • rendering, projecting, or reporting more than the one document resolved by the zero/one/several matrix;
  • scanning later associations when the exact selected-primary-or-first candidate lacks a workable public-safe location;
  • a multi-target Semantic Token schema, link group, display limit, or overflow state;
  • automatic Tag-document creation, repair, deletion, or synchronization;
  • Tag Editor search, membership mutation, or reordering of the complete document association set;
  • a Clear primary action or any other way to return a stored primary to empty without deleting its complete Tag row;
  • using primary_document to block or authorize document Delete, tag_id assignment/reassignment/clear, or Tag deletion;
  • cascading Tag deletion into documents or document deletion/disassociation into Registry primary selection;
  • deriving associations from document titles, content, source proximity, or usage rows;
  • recursive relationship resolution or inferred relationship expansion;
  • a public Tag registry, target lookup, usage index, or client-side resolver;
  • changing document lifecycle because an association appears, disappears, or becomes primary.
